title: Examining Scleritis Content on the Social Media App 'TikTok': A Comprehensive Analysis of Quality, Engagement, and Misinformation
screen_reason: Abstract-only record. Content analysis of TikTok videos retrieved by the scleritis-related search terms, coded into content types including an explicit 'misinformation' category; the conclusion states verbatim that 10.1% contained misinformation, a share of classified items with (an implied) denominator. The PEMAT understandability/actionability means are quality scores reported as means, not shares, so they generate no row.

estimates.measure_type: % of scleritis-related TikTok videos categorised as containing misinformation
estimates.value_raw: 10.1% containing misinformation; the truncated RESULTS sentence reads "= 7) contained misinformation", i.e. 7 videos
estimates.denominator: scleritis-related TikTok videos retrieved with TikTok's search function for 'scleritis', 'anterior scleritis' and 'posterior scleritis'; the total number analysed is not stated in the available abstract (7/10.1% implies roughly 69 videos)
estimates.definition: video assigned to the 'misinformation' category in the content-type coding (informative, misinformation, personal experience, diagnosis, miscellaneous)
estimates.misinfo_def: "potentially misleading or inaccurate content" about a medical topic; operationalised as the content-type category "misinformation"
estimates.n: not stated in the abstract (numerator 7 videos; denominator implied ~69 videos)
estimates.source_quote: CONCLUSION: Most scleritis-related TikToks are from non-medical professionals with 10.1% containing misinformation.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Authors' own content-type categorisation of each video; the abstract names no coders, no external reference standard and no inter-rater reliability. Quality was separately scored with PEMAT-AV.
estimates.moderator_quote: Using TikTok's search function, videos tagged with 'scleritis,' 'anterior scleritis,' and 'posterior scleritis' were analyzed. Videos were categorized by creator type, engagement (views, likes, comments, shares), and content type (informative, misinformation, personal experience, diagnosis, miscellaneous).
estimates.notes: ABSTRACT-ONLY extraction; the Results sentence in the recovered abstract is truncated ('RESULTS: = 7) contained misinformation'), so the denominator is not stated and had to be left as an implied ~69 videos. The 10.1% itself is verbatim in the Conclusion. year is the publication year (2025, from the DOI); the data-collection date is not given. No country is stated; TikTok search is not geographically bounded in the abstract, hence country_norm=Global. denom_selection left blank because the abstract does not say the search was truncated to a top-N or first-page set - if the full paper shows a rank-truncated sample, this should become curated.

missed_or_uncertain: The PEMAT-AV scores (mean understandability 37.0%, actionability 6.0%) are quality scale means over the same videos, not shares of items judged false, so no QUALITY row was created (a Likert/scale mean is not a share; INSTRUCTIONS section 3). The share of videos by creator type ('Most ... are from non-medical professionals') is not a misinformation share. The full Results sentence, and with it the denominator and any breakdown by creator type, is missing from the recovered abstract; the full text should be checked before this row is pooled.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis of TikTok videos retrieved through the platform's own search function on three scleritis terms; number of videos, search date, country and coder details are not reported in the available abstract. Videos categorised by creator type, engagement and content type (including a 'misinformation' category) by the authors, with PEMAT-AV used for understandability/actionability. No inter-rater reliability, no external ground truth and no sampling frame details are reported in the abstract.
